questions.question: Garba dance is a popular dance of which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Garba dance** is a popular folk dance of the state of **Gujarat** in India.
 
• The dance is performed during the **nine-day **Hindu festival of **Navratri,** which celebrates the victory of **good over evil.**
 
• Garba involves circular movements by a group of dancers who move around a central point, accompanied by music played on traditional instruments like **dhol, tabla, and harmonium.**
 
• The dance is characterized by **colorful costumes, rhythmic clapping**, and **energetic footwork**, and is a symbol of the cultural heritage of Gujarat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bihar **is a state in **eastern India **and is known for its rich history and culture. 

 
 
• **Jhumar, Jat Jatin, Kajari and Paika** are some of the folk dances of Bihar.
 
 
 
• **Goa** is a small coastal state in western India and is famous for its beaches, seafood, and nightlife. 
 
 
• Goa has its own unique folk dances like the **Fugdi and Dekhni.**
 
 
 
• **Assam** is a state in northeastern India and is known for its** tea gardens, wildlife, and culture.**
 
 
• The traditional dance forms of Assam include the **Bihu and Sattriya.**

questions.question: Which of the following options best describes the purpose of the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan (PM-SYM) scheme, 2019?

options.text: Provide healthcare services to pregnant women
Provide education loans to financially weak students
Provide pension to unorganised sector workers
Provide financial assistance to small and marginal farmers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is to __**Provide pension to unorganised sector workers.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan** (PM-SYM) scheme is a **pension scheme** for** unorganized sector workers.**
 
• The scheme aims to provide **financial security **to workers in their old age.
 
• Workers between the age of **18-40 years** with a monthly income of less than **Rs. 15,000 **are eligible for the scheme.
 
• The workers have to contribute a small **monthly amount **towards the pension and the government will also contribute an **equal amount.**
 
• The scheme provides a minimum assured pension of **Rs. 3000 per month** to the beneficiaries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana** provides** financial assistance** to **pregnant women** for their healthcare needs.

 
 
• This is a** Direct Bank Transfer** (DBT) program that is sponsored centrally.
 
• Expectant mothers and lactating women receive a financial incentive of **₹ 5,000 **(paid in three installments) immediately into their bank or post office accounts.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Vidya Lakshmi Yojana** provides** education loans** to students.
 
 
• The **Vidya Lakshmi Portal **is a unique platform designed for students who are looking for an education loan.
 
• It prepares applications for **government scholarships and educational loans** and offers students a** single-window electronic platform** to access information. 
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana **provides** insurance coverage **to** farmers** against crop loss or damage due to natural calamities.
 
 
• Beginning with the** Kharif 2016 season**, the **Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare**, New Delhi, introduced this program in India.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most suitable application of rainwater harvesting?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Irrigation.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rainwater harvesting** is the process of **collecting and storing rainwater **for future use.
 
• The most suitable application of rainwater harvesting is** irrigation**, which has the following advantages:
 
• **Reduces water bills:**
 
 
• Irrigation accounts for a significant portion of water usage in **households and industries.**
 
• By using rainwater for irrigation, one can **reduce** their water bills and save money.
 
 
 
• **Conserves water: **
 
 
• **​**Rainwater harvesting helps in conserving water as it reduces the demand for **freshwater**, which is a scarce resource in many regions.
 
 
 
• **Environmentally friendly**:
 
 
• Rainwater harvesting is an environmentally friendly practice as it reduces the strain on freshwater sources and helps in **replenishing groundwater.**
 
 
 
• **Improves soil quality**:
 
 
• Rainwater is free from chemicals and additives, which makes it an ideal source of water for plants.
 
• It also helps in** improving soil quality and fertility.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Using rainwater for cooking is **not **a suitable application of rainwater harvesting as the water may not be suitable for drinking without** proper treatment.**
 
• Using rainwater for pets is** not **a suitable application of rainwater harvesting as the water may contain **harmful bacteria and parasites** that can cause health problems.
 
• Using rainwater for industrial purposes may **not** be feasible as the water quality requirements for industrial processes are often **stringent, **and rainwater may not meet those standards.

questions.question: Which Act declared that British rule in India would end by 30 June 1948?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Act of 1947.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Act of 1947** is also known as the **Indian Independence Act.**
 
• This Act was passed by the** British Parliament **on **July 18, 1947**, and received royal assent on **July 18, 1947**.
 
• The Act provided for the end of British rule in India and the partition of India into two separate countries,** India and Pakistan.**
 
• The Act also provided for the establishment of two independent dominions, India and Pakistan, within the** British Commonwealth of Nations.**
 
• The Act came into effect on** August 15, 1947, **and marked the **end of British colonial rule **in India after almost **200 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Act of 1858 **is also known as the **Government of India Act**.

 
 
• It transferred the administration of India from the **East India Company to the British Crown**.
 
 
 
• **Act of 1892** is the **Indian Councils Act.**
 
 
• It expanded the** legislative councils **and provided for the election of some members.
 
 
 
• **Act of 1961** is the **Indian Citizenship Act.**
 
 
• **It **provided for the** acquisition and terminatio**n of Indian citizenship.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of articles is related with the feature of Emergency Provisions in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**352 to 360.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Emergency Provisions** in the Indian Constitution are related to the articles** 352 to 360.**
 
• These provisions allow the central government to take control of the state government in case of an emergency situation like **war, external aggression or armed rebellion.**
 
• Article 352 deals with the **proclamation of emergency,** while articles 353 to 355 outline the **effect of the emergency** on the powers of the central government, state government, and the fundamental rights of citizens.
 
• Article 356 empowers the President to dismiss a state government and** impose the President's rule **in case of failure of constitutional machinery in a state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Articles 309 to 312 **deal with the provisions related to the recruitment and conditions of service of persons serving the** Union or a State.**
 
• **Articles 343 to 351** deal with the provisions related to the **official language** of the Union and the States.
 
• **Articles 330 to 342 **deals with the provisions related to the representation of the **Anglo-Indian community **in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.

questions.question: The dividends received by the Government from Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) are ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**non-tax revenue receipts.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dividends** received by the **Government** from **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)** are considered as **non-tax revenue receipts.**
 
• **Non-tax revenue** receipts are the revenue generated by the government through means other than taxes, such as **dividends, profits, fees, and fines.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Capital expenditure** refers to the expenses incurred by the government for the **creation of assets** such as buildings, machinery, etc.

 
 
• Capex is mostly a **one-time investment** in **non-consumable assets** used to support a company's future expansion and preserve current operating levels.
 
 
 
• **Capital receipts** are the receipts of the government that lead to an increase in its** assets and liabilities,** such as borrowings, disinvestment, and recovery of loans.
 
 
• They also make mention of **cash inflows.**
 
• Both **debt and non-debt receipts** are considered capital receipts.
 
 
 
• **Tax revenue receipts** are the revenue generated by the government through taxes such as** income tax, GST, etc. **
 
 
• They come from either **indirect or direct taxes**.
 
• It is the primary source of the **government's regular revenue.****​**

questions.question:
Choose the correct option in the context of given sentences.

**Assertion: **Self-help groups (SHGs) have emerged as an effective model for microfinance in India.

**Reason:** SHGs are able to pool resources and negotiate better loan terms with microfinance institutions.

options.text: Both assertion and reason are true, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.
Both assertion and reason are false.
Both assertion and reason are true, but the reason is NOT the correct explanation of the assertion.
The assertion is true, but the reason is false.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both assertion and reason are true, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.**__
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The assertion that SHGs have emerged as an **effective model for microfinance** in India is **true.**
 
• The reason given to support the assertion is also** true** - SHGs are able to pool resources and negotiate** better loan terms** with microfinance institutions.
 
• Furthermore, SHGs are often better suited to meet the** financial needs of low-income individuals and communities,** compared to traditional banking institutions.

 
• **Microfinance** is the provision of financial services to **low-income individuals or groups **who typically lack access to traditional banking services.
 
• **Self-help groups** (SHGs) are community-based organizations comprising **10-20 members,** usually women, who pool their savings and lend to each other.
 
• SHGs have gained popularity in India as a means of providing **microfinance due to their ability** to negotiate better loan terms and their focus on **financial education** and** the empowerment of women.**

questions.question: When the rate of interest is at its maximum, which of the following will follow?

options.text: The demand for bonds will be at its minimum.
The speculative demand for money will be zero.
The speculative demand for money will be at its maximum.
The speculative demand for money will be equal to the supply of money.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The speculative demand for money will be zero.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

 
• When the rate of interest is at its** maximum**, it becomes expensive to **borrow money**, which reduces the demand for **loans and investments.**
 
• As a result, the speculative demand for money** becomes zero** because there are fewer opportunities for **profitable investments**.
 
• The demand for bonds may also** decrease as investors **may prefer to hold onto their cash instead of investing in fixed-income securities.
 
• The **speculative demand** for money decreases when the **interest rates are high.**
 
• The supply of money is** not affected **by the interest rates and is determined by the central bank.
 
• **Speculative demand** for money refers to the **demand for money** that is held for the purpose of making speculative investments or taking advantage of future opportunities.
 
• **Demand for bonds** refers to the demand for** fixed-income securities** that pay a fixed rate of interest over a set period of time.

questions.question: Which of the following laws states that "The magnitude of the induced EMF in a circuit is equal to the time rate of change of magnetic flux through the circuit"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Faraday's law.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction** states that the magnitude of the** induced EMF** (Electromotive Force) in a circuit is equal to the time **rate of change of magnetic flux** through the circuit.
 
• This law was discovered by** Michael Faraday** in **1831** and is one of the fundamental laws of **electromagnetism.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coulomb's law** is a law of** electrostatics** that states that the force between **two charged particles** is proportional to the **product of their charges** and inversely proportional to the **square of the distance** between them.
 
• **Kirchhoff's laws **are two laws that describe the behavior of **electrical circuits**: Kirchhoff's current law states that the total current entering a junction in a circuit must equal the **total current leaving the junction**, while Kirchhoff's voltage law states that the** sum of the voltages** around any closed loop in a circuit must equal zero.
 
• **Laplace's law **is a law of hydrodynamics that describes the relationship between** pressure, surface tension, and curvature** in a liquid.

questions.question: The number of elements known at the time of Russian chemist Dmitri Ivanovich Mendeleev was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**63.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The number of elements known at the time of **Mendeleev **was **63.**
 
• This is because Mendeleev's periodic table included **63 elements,** arranged in order of increasing **atomic mass.**
 
• Some of the elements he predicted, such as **gallium and germanium,** were discovered later and found to fit into the gaps he had left in the table.
 
• Today, we know of **118 elements** in total, with the most recent additions being **nihonium, moscovium, tennessine, and oganesson**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dmitri Ivanovich Mendeleev** is known for creating the **first periodic table** of elements.
 
• He arranged the elements based on their **atomic mass** and observed that there was a **periodicity** in their properties.
 
• **Mendeleev **predicted the existence of some elements that were yet to be discovered, and left gaps in his periodic table for them.
 
• **57** is the number of elements known at the time of Swedish chemist **Jundefinedns Jacob Berzelius**, who is known for discovering several new elements and developing the modern system of chemical symbols.
 
• **53** is the number of elements known at the time of English chemist** John Dalton**, who is known for developing the atomic theory of matter.
 
• **67** is the number of elements known at the time of American chemist **Glenn T. Seaborg, **who discovered several new elements and contributed to the development of the actinide series of elements.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the objectives of the 'Swadesh Darshan 2.0 Scheme'?

options.text: To provide vocational training to youth
To enhance the contribution of farming
To increase private sector investment in tourism and hospitality
To promote local art and culture handicrafts and cuisines etc.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To increase private sector investment in tourism and hospitality.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

• The objective of the **'Swadesh Darshan 2.0 Scheme**' is to increase** private sector investment** in tourism and hospitality.
 
• The scheme aims to develop theme-based** tourist circuits **and promote **tourism infrastructure** in the country.
 
• The focus is on developing and promoting lesser-known destinations and creating employment opportunities in the **tourism sector.**
 
• **'Swadesh Darshan 2.0 Scheme'** is a part of the government's larger initiative to boost tourism in India, which includes the** 'Atithi Devo Bhava'** campaign and the **'Incredible India'** campaign.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Ministry of Tourism** initiated the **"National Mission on Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Augmentation Drive** (PRASAD)" in 2014–15 with the goal of **developing pilgrimage** locations holistically.
 
• The PRASHAD Scheme aims to enhance the religious tourism experience by identifying and developing **pilgrimage sites **throughout India.
 
• In order to offer a comprehensive religious** tourism experience,** it seeks to integrate pilgrimage sites in a **planned, sustainable, and prioritized manner.**
